chunks: And by this chain of narration. He said:
Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said: The qunut in witr is like your qunut on Friday. You say in the supplication of the qunut:

O Allah! Your light was perfected so You guided, so praise be to You, our Lord. You stretched out Your hand so You gave, so praise be to You, our Lord. Your forbearance became great so You pardoned, and praise be to You, our Lord. Your face is the most noble of faces, Your direction is the best of directions, Your gift is the most excellent of gifts and the most pleasant. You are obeyed, our Lord, so You give thanks; You are disobeyed, our Lord, yet You forgive whomever You wish. You answer the desperate, You remove harm, You heal the sick, and You deliver from the great distress. No one can repay Your favors, and no speech of any speaker can enumerate Your blessings.

O Allah! To You gazes were raised, feet were moved, necks were stretched, hands were lifted, and supplications were made with tongues, and judgment was sought from You regarding deeds. Our Lord! Forgive us and have mercy on us, and judge between us and Your creation with truth — You are the best of those who judge.

O Allah! To You we complain about the absence of our Prophet, the severity of the time upon us, the occurrence of trials, the gathering of enemies, the great number of our enemy, and our small number. So relieve all of that, O Lord, with a victory from You that You hasten, and a help from You that You strengthen, and a just Imam that You make appear — O God of Truth, Lord of the worlds.

Then say in the qunut of witr after this: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him' seventy times, and seek refuge in Allah from the Fire many times. And say after completing the witr following the taslim: 'Glory be to my Lord, the King, the Holy, the Almighty, the All-Wise' three times. 'Praise be to the Lord of the morning, praise be to the Splitter of the daybreak' three times.

key_terms.آلاء: Ala' (pl. ala') — divine favors, blessings, graces
key_terms.إمام عدل: Imam of justice — a just divinely-appointed leader; in Shia theology, refers to the awaited Imam
key_terms.القنوت: Qunut — a supplication recited during certain prayer positions, especially standing after ruku' or in the last rak'ah
key_terms.المضطر: Al-mudtarr — one in dire need, desperate; refers to the one who has no recourse but God
key_terms.الوتر: Witr — the odd-number concluding prayer of the night vigil, considered highly recommended (mustahabb)

ai.seo_question: What is the qunut supplication for witr prayer according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) teaches the qunut supplication for the witr prayer, which mirrors the Friday qunut. This comprehensive du'a praises God's attributes through His actions (guiding, giving, forgiving), acknowledges human helplessness before His blessings, then turns to communal supplication for relief from adversity and the appearance of the just Imam. The hadith was transmitted during the early Abbasid period, when Shia communities faced political persecution, making the prayer for a 'just Imam' (إمام عدل) a pointed theological statement about legitimate rule.
